title: ehos.yaml/v3
description: What a workload needs in order to run, as its developer states it (D-51). A released version is frozen: this file is never edited, and any change is a new version.

schema.description: The version of this format the file is written in. A file without it is refused, never guessed at.

application.description: Which of the project's contract domains this image is: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter and not ending with a dash, and not `ehos`. Only a project whose contracts declare more than one domain names it; otherwise the generator takes the name from the one domain.

needs.description: What the workload needs from the environment it runs in. A workload may need nothing.

database.description: A PostgreSQL schema of its own, on the resource its environment binds it to (D-54).

version.description: The PostgreSQL major version: `16` for exactly 16, `>= 16` for 16 or later. Without it, any version the resource runs.

migrate.description: The command and its arguments, run before the workload starts, as the schema's owner. Without it, no migration runs.

people.description: Present when the workload reads the company's people from EHOS, by itself, through EHOS's API (D-81): `read` is the only value. The reading waits until someone who manages people agrees, and the workload is given the key it identifies itself with, whether or not it signs people in.

serves.description: Each endpoint that listens, public or not. A workload may listen on nothing but its health port. Names and ports are unique, and no port is the health port: EHOS checks these beside the schema.

sign_in.description: Present when the workload signs people in through EHOS (D-64, D-69): `{}` for its own application only, `applications` for the others its pages get credentials for. It needs an entry `web` that is public, where sign-in returns (D-68): EHOS checks this beside the schema.

applications.description: The other applications its pages get credentials for, by name, each once and not its own. An application's side agrees before any credential for it is issued (D-64).

health.description: Where EHOS probes the workload. EHOS never starts a workload it cannot probe, and never exposes this port.

port.description: The port EHOS probes on. It is never exposed, and no entry of `serves` may use it.

ready.description: The HTTP path, starting with a slash, that answers 2xx once the workload can serve.

live.description: The HTTP path, starting with a slash, that answers 2xx while the workload is not stuck.

name.description: The endpoint's name, which is also a Kubernetes port name: lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter, at most 15 characters. `web` gets the application's own host; any other public one gets `<application>-<name>` (D-55).

public.description: Whether the endpoint asks to be reachable from outside the installation. A request: EHOS decides whether to expose it.

port.description: A TCP port the workload listens on, from 1024 to 65535.
